senses.gloss: (b. h.) [to swing] to be light, slender, unimportant.—Part. קַל.
units: Snh. VI, 5 (ref. to קללת, Deut. XXI, 23) בזמן … קַלַּנִי מראשי וכ׳ when man suffers punishment, what does the Shekhinah say? ‘I am lighter than my head, than my arm’ (euphem. for, I feel my head heavy &c.); Y. ib. 23ᵈ bot. אנן תנינן קַלֵּינִי (= קל איני) we read ḳalleni, I am not lighter; אית תניי תני קל אני some Tannai reads ḳal ăni; מאן דאמר קליני לית הוא אלא קליל according to him that reads ḳalleni, it is a euphemistic expression for ‘light’ (i.e. my head is light, I feel giddy; my arm is light, I feel weak); מאן דאמר קלני … נטיל according to the version ḳallani, it is a euphemistic expression for ‘heavy’ (i.e. my head, my arm is heavy); Bab. ib. 46ᵇ Abbayi says כמאן דאמר קל לית (read ḳalleni) as one says, ‘light (I am) not’ (i.e. I feel heavy, without euphemism)—(which is refuted by Raba, who explains the word in question) קליל לי עלמא, v. קַלִּיל II.
<cite ref="Moed Katan 17b:15">M. Kat. 17ᵇ</cite> <he>הכביד … מֵיקַל וכ׳</he> if the mourner’s hair is too heavy, he may make it lighter with a razor; Y. ib. III, 82ᵃ top.
Erub. IV, 9 להָקֵל על העשיר to make it easy for the rich man; a. fr.—Trnsf. ה׳ ראשו to be irreverent, talk frivolously (v. קַלּוּת).
<cite ref="Mishnah Berakhot 9:5">Ber. IX, 5</cite> <he>לא יָקֵל אדם את ראשו כנגד וכ׳</he> man (a pilgrim coming to Jerusalem) must not behave irreverently in sight of the eastern gate &c.

<cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 24">Yalk. Gen. 24</cite> <he>מֵיקֶלֶת ראשה</he> she is frivolous (light-minded); <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Nach 265">Yalk. Is. 265</cite> <he>מֵקֶילֶת ראש</he>; (<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 18:2">Gen. R. s. 18</cite> <he>מיקרת</he>, v. <cite ref="J00580"><he>יָקַר</he></cite>).

senses.gloss: to be lenient; to incline towards the less restrictive practice, opp. החמיר, v. חָמַר I. Y. M. Kat. l. c. הלכה כדברי מי שהוא מיקל the adopted practice follows the opinion of him who is more lenient; Erub. 46ᵃ, a. fr. כדברי המיקל וכ׳.
units: <cite ref="Yevamot 88a:10">Yeb. 88ᵃ</cite> <he>הֵיקַלְתָּ עליה</he>, v. <cite ref="H01218"><he>חָמַר</he> I</cite>.

<cite ref="Pesachim 52b">Pes. 52ᵇ</cite>, v. <cite ref="M00151"><he>מַגִּיד</he></cite>. Erub. l. c. wherever you find <he>יחיד מיקל ורבים וכ׳</he> an individual scholar favoring the more lenient practice against several in favor of restriction.
<cite ref="Shabbat 129a">Sabb. 129ᵃ</cite>, a. fr. <he>ספק נפשות להָקל</he> where there is a doubt involving the endangering of human life, the more lenient rule is applied; a. fr.

<cite ref="Shabbat 129a">Ib.</cite> <he>כל המיקל … מְקִילִין לו מזוניתיו וכ׳</he> he that stints himself at the meal taken after blood-letting, to him they in heaven will give his sustenance stintingly; a. e.
<cite ref="Mishnah Ketubot 7:6">Keth. VII, 6</cite> <he>מְקַלֶּלֶת</he>, v. <cite ref="J00187"><he>יִוֹלֵד</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Shabbat 62b:13">Sabb. 62ᵇ</cite> <he>שאשתו מְקַלַּלְתּוֹ בפניו</he> whom his wife curses in his presence.

<cite ref="Pesachim 87b:17">Pes. 87ᵇ</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Proverbs 30:10">Prov. XXX, 10</cite> sq.) <he>אפו׳ דור שאביו יְקַלֵּל וכ׳</he> even if it be a generation of men that curse their father …, do not denounce &c.
<cite ref="Yoma 75a:4">Yoma 75ᵃ</cite> <he>ק׳ את הנחש וכ׳</he> God cursed the serpent, yet it climbs up the roof and finds its food.

<cite ref="Sotah 11a:14">Sot. 11ᵃ</cite> (expl. <he>ועלה</he>, <cite ref="Exodus 1:10">Ex. I, 10</cite>, as euphem. for <he>ועלינו</he>) <he>כאדם שמְקַלֵּל את עצמו וכ׳</he> like a man that wants to curse himself (express an ill omen about himself), and hangs his curse on others.

<cite ref="Bava Batra 88b:10">B. Bath. 88ᵇ</cite> <he>הקב״ה בירך … וקִלְּלָן וכ׳</he> the Lord blessed Israel with the twenty-two letters of the alphabet (from <cite ref="A00000"><he>א</he></cite> of <he>אם</he>, <cite ref="Leviticus 26:3">Lev. XXVI, 3</cite>, to <cite ref="V00000"><he>ת</he></cite> of <he>קוממיות</he>, <cite ref="Leviticus 26:13">ib. 13</cite>), and cursed them with eight letters (from <cite ref="F00000"><he>ו</he></cite> of <he>ואם</he>, ib. 14, to <he>ם</he> of <he>נפשם</he>, ib. 43).

<cite ref="Sanhedrin 70a:19">Snh. 70ᵃ</cite> <he>מתוך שקלקלו … קִלְּלוֹ ברביעי</he> because Ham injured him by (preventing his begetting) a fourth son, he (Noah) cursed him by his fourth son (Canaan).

<cite ref="Sanhedrin 91b:18">Ib. 91ᵇ</cite> <he>כל המונע … שבמעי אמן מְקַלְּלִין אותו</he> (not <he>אמו</he>) he that withholds a tradition from his pupil, even the embryos in their mother’s womb will curse him; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Nach 947:26">Yalk. Prov. 947</cite>; a. fr.

<cite ref="Berakhot 61a:10">Ber. 61ᵃ</cite> <he>בתחלה נ׳ … נִתְקַלְּלָה וכ׳</he> the serpent was cursed first, and then Eve &c.; <cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 20">Gen. R. s. 20</cite>; <cite ref="Eruvin 18a:18">Erub. 18ᵃ</cite>.
<cite ref="Eruvin 18b:18">Ib. 18ᵇ</cite> <he>נתקללה בבל נִתְקַלְּלוּ וכ׳</he> when Babylon was cursed, her neighbors were cursed.
<cite ref="Bekhorot 8a:15">Bekh. 8ᵃ</cite> <he>אם מבהמה נתקללה וכ׳</he> if she (Eve) was cursed (with prolonged pregnancy) more than cattle &c.
<cite ref="Bekhorot 8a">Ib.</cite> <he>נ׳ הוא … אחת לשבע</he> it (the serpent) was cursed seven times more than certain cattle.
Ib. נ׳ הוא מחיה (not נתקלקל); a. fr.—[Tosef. Sot. II, 3 ניקללה ניוולה, Var. ניקל, read: ניקתה בניוולה, v. נָקָה Nif.]
